Retrieve Bank of Japan series metadata

Source: R/metadata.R
boj_metadata.Rd

Retrieves and parses the official BOJ getMetadata CSV for one database. The Japanese metadata route is the canonical bilingual source: it carries both Japanese (*_J) and English fields. Use search_boj_series() for bounded discovery in a large catalogue, especially the Tankan CO database, rather than eagerly materialising that database by default.

Usage

boj_metadata(
  db,
  language = "both",
  cache_dir = boj_cache_dir(),
  refresh = FALSE,
  offline = FALSE,
  max_age = 24 * 60 * 60,
  timeout = 60,
  retries = 3L,
  wait = 1,
  max_bytes = 128 * 1024^2,
  max_rows = 50000L,
  allow_large = FALSE,
  include_groups = TRUE,
  deadline = NULL
)

Arguments

db

A BOJ database identifier, such as "FM08". It is converted to uppercase after validation; an identifier with a syntactically valid shape can still be rejected by the BOJ API if that database is not available.

language

Output language: "both", "en", or "jp". "both" retains paired Japanese and English text fields; "en" and "jp" retain only the requested language's name, unit, category and notes.

cache_dir

Character path to the snapshot cache. The default is boj_cache_dir(), which uses the readboj.cache_dir option or tools::R_user_dir("readboj", "cache"). Missing cache subdirectories are created as needed.

refresh

Logical flag. When TRUE, bypasses a current cached request snapshot and obtains a fresh response. It is validated even when offline = TRUE.

offline

Logical flag. When TRUE, requires a valid cached snapshot and makes no network request. It is useful for deterministic replay.

max_age

Non-negative number of seconds for which a cached snapshot is considered current; Inf permits any age. The default is 24 hours.

timeout

Non-negative per-request timeout in seconds. The default for metadata requests is 60 seconds.

retries

Non-negative whole number of retries for transient transport or HTTP failures. The default is 3; non-transient failures are not retried.

wait

Non-negative number of seconds used between pages, code batches and retries. It is skipped for offline reads and is bounded by deadline.

max_bytes

Positive maximum decompressed response bytes per page. The default is 128 MiB; oversized responses fail with readboj_size_error before parsing or caching.

max_rows

Positive whole-number maximum metadata rows materialised, including hierarchy groups before include_groups filtering. The default is 50,000; exceeding it raises readboj_size_error.

allow_large

Logical flag. TRUE explicitly permits eager CO (Tankan) materialisation, subject to max_rows, byte, timeout and deadline bounds. The default is FALSE.

include_groups

Logical flag. TRUE (the default) keeps hierarchy heading rows, which have an empty series_code and is_series = FALSE; FALSE filters them out after parsing.

deadline

An optional absolute POSIXct/POSIXlt deadline shared by the metadata request, retries and delays. A bounded default is created when omitted.

Value

A base data.frame in BOJ source order, with row names reset, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, and a readboj_provenance attribute. For language = "both", columns are in this exact order: db, series_code, name_jp, name_en, unit_jp, unit_en, frequency, category_jp, category_en, layer1, layer2, layer3, layer4, layer5, start_time, end_time, last_update, notes_jp, notes_en, and is_series. The first two columns and all text fields are character; layer1–layer5 are integer; last_update is Date; and is_series is logical. For language = "en", the Japanese name, unit, category and notes columns are removed; for language = "jp", the English counterparts are removed. Thus the retained language fields preserve the corresponding column order from the bilingual schema. start_time and end_time are source period labels as character. Provenance records the canonical and final URLs, raw hash, retrieval/cache identity, transfer encoding, BOJ date/message ID, selected database and language, parser schema and package version.

Details

language = "both" and language = "jp" request the Japanese CSV (CP932) so that paired fields are available; language = "en" requests the English CSV (UTF-8) and removes Japanese columns from the result. Metadata is read in source order. With include_groups = TRUE, hierarchy heading rows without a series code are retained and have is_series = FALSE; setting it to FALSE retains only rows with a non-empty series code.

A CO request is rejected before downloading unless allow_large = TRUE. That opt-in does not remove the independent max_rows materialisation bound. Responses are fetched over HTTPS from the official BOJ host and successfully cached as content-addressed snapshots. A current snapshot is reused unless refresh = TRUE; offline = TRUE requires a valid matching snapshot and makes no network request. See read_boj_series() for the common cache, retry, timeout, and deadline controls.

Errors and side effects

Invalid parameters, an unavailable large database, malformed or changed CSV schema, API errors, row limits, transport failures and missing offline snapshots raise typed readboj_*_error conditions. The function may perform network I/O and create cache files below cache_dir; temporary files are cleaned up and no package startup download occurs.

Examples

# This small installed fixture is synthetic and makes no network request.
metadata_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata-bilingual-utf8.csv", package = "readboj"
)
metadata <- read_boj_snapshot(
  metadata_path, type = "metadata_csv", db = "FM08", encoding = "UTF-8"
)
metadata[c("series_code", "name_en", "name_jp", "is_series")]
#>   series_code                 name_en      name_jp is_series
#> 1                   Synthetic heading     合成階層     FALSE
#> 2    SYNTHM01 Synthetic monthly index 合成月次指数      TRUE
#> 3    SYNTHM02  Synthetic monthly rate 合成月次金利      TRUE

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  boj_metadata(
    "FM08", language = "both", include_groups = FALSE,
    cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache"),
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 8 * 1024^2,
    max_rows = 100L
  )
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.")
}
#> Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.
